reason: The text contains two primary human characters, Adam (האדם) and Eve (the woman/חוה), who are regular people characters. Both have spoken lines: Adam declares 'This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh' and later responds to God's questions; Eve speaks with the serpent saying 'From the fruit of the trees of the garden we may eat,' and the text describes her reasoning and desire regarding the forbidden fruit ('the tree was good for food... a delight to the eyes'). Both characters demonstrate emotions—Adam and Eve experience shame when their eyes are opened and hide from God—and both express opinions about their circumstances (Adam recognizes Eve as a suitable helper; Eve reasons about the attractiveness and desirability of the tree for gaining wisdom).
